options.text: the fall in average cost per unit as the scale of production expands
the total savings a firm keeps in the bank
the rise in total cost as more output is produced
the reduction in the number of workers employed by a firm

questions.explanation: Economies of scale are about cost per unit, not total cost. Total cost normally rises with output; what falls is the average cost of each unit, which is why large firms can undercut small ones.

distractorRationale.b: Bank savings are a financial holding, unrelated to the cost of production
distractorRationale.c: Total cost rising with output is normal and is not an economy at all
distractorRationale.d: Cutting the workforce is retrenchment; economies of scale usually accompany expansion

questions.stem: A firm obtains a bank loan at a lower rate of interest than smaller rivals because of its size. This is an example of a

options.text: technical economy of scale
financial economy of scale
external economy of scale
managerial diseconomy of scale

questions.explanation: Cheaper access to capital because of size and creditworthiness is a financial economy, and it is internal because it arises from the growth of this firm alone rather than of the industry.

distractorRationale.a: Technical economies come from large specialised plant and machinery
distractorRationale.c: External economies are shared by all firms in the industry or locality, which a private loan rate is not
distractorRationale.d: A diseconomy raises unit cost; this saving lowers it

questions.stem: Which of the following is an external economy of scale?

options.text: A firm buys raw materials in bulk and receives a discount
A technical college opens in the town and trains workers for the whole industry
A firm employs a specialist accountant and a specialist marketer
A firm installs a large automated machine

questions.explanation: The trained workers are available to every firm in the locality, so the saving flows from the growth of the industry rather than of any one firm. That shared nature is the test of an external economy.

distractorRationale.a: Bulk-buying discounts are internal marketing economies enjoyed by that firm alone
distractorRationale.c: Employing specialist managers is an internal managerial economy
distractorRationale.d: Installing large plant is an internal technical economy

questions.stem: The optimum size of a firm is the size at which

options.text: total output is highest
long-run average cost per unit is lowest
the firm employs the largest number of workers
total revenue is highest

questions.explanation: Optimum here means most efficient, and efficiency is measured by cost per unit. Beyond that point diseconomies of scale begin to push average cost back up, even though output may still be rising.

distractorRationale.a: The largest output may be produced at wasteful cost per unit
distractorRationale.c: Employment size says nothing about cost efficiency
distractorRationale.d: Maximum revenue ignores cost and is a different objective altogether

questions.stem: Which of the following best illustrates an internal diseconomy of scale?

options.text: Traffic congestion in the industrial estate raises delivery times for all firms
Decisions in a very large firm are delayed by many layers of management
Local rents rise because many firms compete for land
Competition among firms in the area bids up wages

questions.explanation: Bureaucratic delay arises inside the firm as a direct result of its own growth, and it raises that firm's costs. The other three options raise costs for every firm in the area, so they are external diseconomies.

distractorRationale.a: Congestion affects all firms in the locality, making it external
distractorRationale.c: Rising rents are a locality-wide effect and therefore external
distractorRationale.d: Wage competition among local firms is likewise an external diseconomy

questions.stem: Cement factories in Nigeria are located at Ewekoro, Sokoto and Obajana mainly because of

options.text: nearness to the largest consumer markets
nearness to limestone deposits
the availability of seaports for export
the mild climate of those areas

questions.explanation: Limestone is bulky and loses much of its weight in processing, so it is far cheaper to carry the finished cement to the market than to haul raw limestone to a distant factory. Industries using such weight-losing raw materials locate at the source.

distractorRationale.a: Lagos and other large markets are not where these plants sit; market pull dominates only for bulky or perishable finished goods
distractorRationale.c: Nigerian cement is produced mainly for the domestic market, and Obajana and Sokoto are far inland
distractorRationale.d: Climate matters for agriculture and a few processes, not for cement making

questions.stem: The deliberate dispersal of industries away from a congested area to other parts of the country is called

options.text: localisation
delocalisation
diversification
integration

questions.explanation: Delocalisation reverses the concentration created by localisation, usually through incentives such as tax holidays and industrial estates, so as to spread employment and relieve congestion.

distractorRationale.a: Localisation is the concentration of an industry in one area, the opposite of what is described
distractorRationale.c: Diversification means widening the range of products or activities a firm undertakes
distractorRationale.d: Integration means the combination of firms, whether horizontally or vertically

questions.stem: External economies of scale are enjoyed by all firms in an industry, not only by the firm that expands.

options.text: True
False

questions.explanation: True. External economies flow from the growth of the industry or the locality — a pool of skilled labour, specialist suppliers, shared infrastructure — so any firm operating there benefits, regardless of its own size.

distractorRationale.b: This describes internal economies, which are confined to the expanding firm itself
